 Professional Computing Resources (PCR) supports complex, regulated organizations, especially higher education and the public sector, with technology asset management solutions across hardware and telecom.
 Orbit is PCR’s new cloud product for software lifecycle management. Orbit unifies software spend, usage, renewals, vendor contracts, and ROI insights into a single system of record, paired with an AI powered layer that helps teams surface what matters and what to do next.
 Orbit has a strong runway through PCR’s installed base, with a large horizontal opportunity beyond it. Orbit is the starting point, not the finish line. We intend to keep shipping modules and adjacent products over time to address more of the IT workflow in higher ed and the public sector, leveraging PCR’s distribution and Valsoft’s operational strength to move quickly.
 The role
 We’re hiring a Head of Revenue to lead Orbit’s go to market from launch through early scale. This is the first dedicated commercial hire for Orbit. You will own pipeline creation, run full cycle deals, and build the repeatable sales motion we will scale over time.
 This is a hands on operator role. You will be a key bridge between the market and product, turning customer discovery into clear requirements, prioritization, and shipped capabilities that drive adoption and profitable growth. You will also continuously look for ways to grow Orbit and expand the opportunity, both by extending Orbit into adjacent workflows and by identifying new modules or product opportunities beyond Orbit that fit the higher ed and public sector IT workflow where PCR already plays today.
 As traction grows, we will add tools and capacity such as marketing support, SDR support, and partners, but early on you will be the person driving momentum.
 What you’ll do and own
 1) Own revenue end to end, hands on
 Own new revenue for Orbit and take a hands on approach to closing business
 Build pipeline through targeted outbound, webinars and events, partnerships, and leveraging PCR’s installed base
 Run deals end to end from discovery to demo to pilot or proof to proposal to negotiation to close
 Sell to cross functional stakeholders and buying committees across IT, procurement, finance, and operations
 Maintain strong CRM hygiene, forecasting, and a consistent weekly operating cadence for pipeline reviews and deal strategy
 2) Build demand in a scrappy, repeatable way
 Create and run outbound motions including account lists, sequencing, messaging tests, and a call email LinkedIn mix
 Develop campaigns that create spikes in demand such as webinars, customer showcases, partner sessions, and conference follow ups
 Establish a simple measurable funnel and iterate quickly using conversion rates, cycle length, and win loss themes
 Use PCR’s credibility, relationships, and customer access to accelerate trust and shorten cycles
 3) Translate market feedback into shipped must haves
 Spend meaningful time in customer conversations to understand workflows, blockers, and urgency drivers
 Turn insights into structured inputs for product and engineering including requirements, prioritization, integrations, packaging, and what needs to be true to win and expand
 Partner closely with product and engineering to sharpen workflows and push fast iterations that improve conversion, adoption, and retention
 Create early proof points such as reference customers, case studies, and outcome narratives
 4) Keep expanding the opportunity, Orbit and beyond
 Continuously look for opportunities to expand Orbit into adjacent needs across the higher ed and public sector IT workflow where PCR plays today
 Identify and validate new modules, integrations, and next products through discovery, then help turn the best opportunities into a clear build and sell plan
 Bring a GM mindset to growth by increasing ACV, improving retention and expansion, and strengthening Orbit’s strategic position over the next three to five years

 Create the repeatable sales playbook including ICP, messaging, talk tracks, demo narrative, objection handling, sequences, and lightweight enablement
 Recommend when to add capacity such as SDR, marketing support, partners, and CS based on leading indicators and what is proven
 Help define the longer term commercial approach including coverage model, partner strategy, and the operating cadence that scales

 6 to 12 plus years in B2B SaaS revenue roles with full cycle closing experience

 Strong discovery, presentation, negotiation, and written communication skills
 High ownership and operational discipline, you run a tight cadence, keep deals moving, and improve the system
 Experience in a startup, early stage, or bootstrapped environment where you wore multiple hats and built GTM foundations
 Demonstrated ability to work with product, identify product opportunities from customer feedback, and translate them into must haves with product and engineering
 Experience launching a new product or building a repeatable motion from scratch
 Nice to haves
 Higher ed, public sector, or healthcare experience
 Familiarity with ITSM, ITAM, SAM, procurement, vendor management, or contract lifecycle concepts
 Partnership or channel experience with resellers, associations, consultants, or ISV partners
 AI curiosity and comfort positioning AI enabled workflows credibly with practical value, not buzzwords
 Compensation
 Base salary plus bonus tied to value creation in Orbit, specifically profitable MRR growth, with a ramp period and milestone based accelerators aligned to early stage execution.

 Remote friendly, with travel for key customer meetings, conferences, and relationship building as needed.

 8am à 4pm pendant formation d'une durée d'environ 3 mois

 Environnement de travail 
 Milieu stimulant axé sur l'innovation et l'amélioration continue.
 Équipe collaborative et expérimentée.
 Possibilités de développement professionnel.
 Votre rôle 
 À titre d'électronicien(ne), vous serez responsable de l'installation, de l'entretien, du dépannage et de la réparation des équipements électriques et électroniques de l'usine.
 Principales responsabilités
 Diagnostiquer les pannes et déterminer leurs causes à l'aide d'instruments de mesure et de contrôle.
 Inspecter les moteurs, générateurs, disjoncteurs et autres équipements électriques afin de détecter toute anomalie (vibrations, bruits ou surchauffe).
 Effectuer le démontage, la réparation, le remontage et les essais des installations et composants électriques.
 Analyser, vérifier et réparer les équipements, circuits et systèmes de contrôle électroniques.
 Participer à l'installation et, au besoin, à la fabrication de composantes électriques destinées à de nouvelles machines ou équipements.
 Lire et interpréter les plans, schémas électriques, procédures de travail et documents techniques.
 Réaliser les mesures et essais requis à l'aide d'instruments spécialisés.
 Compléter la documentation technique, les rapports d'activités et les fiches d'autocontrôle.
 Utiliser les outils et équipements appropriés de façon sécuritaire et efficace.
 Installer et maintenir les dispositifs de prévention des accidents et de protection.
 Effectuer la manutention de pièces à l'aide d'équipements de levage tels que palans, potences, transpalettes et ponts roulants.
 Participer aux activités de réception, d'expédition et d'inventaire du matériel de son secteur.
 Maintenir un environnement de travail propre, sécuritaire et conforme aux normes établies.
 Réaliser les activités de consignation et de cadenassage lors des interventions nécessitant une coupure d'énergie.
 Procéder au démontage et au remontage de composantes mécaniques, électriques ou électroniques liées aux équipements de production.

 Formation
 DEC en électronique (option électrodynamique) ou formation équivalente.
 Certificat de compétence en électricité (License C - hors construction/ Certificat de compétence en électricité (CÉ).
 Compétences
 Capacité démontrée à diagnostiquer avec précision les défaillances électriques et électroniques.
 Solides compétences en dépannage, réparation et entretien d'équipements industriels.
 Atouts 
 Expérience dans un environnement manufacturier ou industriel.
 Connaissance des systèmes de contrôle industriels.
 Expérience avec les moteurs, générateurs et équipements électromécaniques.
 Connaissance des procédures de cadenassage et des normes de santé et sécurité.
 Qualités personnelles recherchées 
 Esprit d'analyse et rigueur technique.
 Autonomie et sens des responsabilités.
 Habileté à travailler en équipe.
 Souci de la qualité et de la sécurité.
 Capacité à gérer les priorités dans un environnement dynamique.
 Poste syndiqué 
 Ce poste est couvert par l'accréditation syndicale et est régi par les termes et conditions de la Convention collective des travailleurs des Énergies renouvelables – CSN .
 Prêt(e) à relever le défi? Joignez-vous à GE Vernova et participez à la création de solutions énergétiques durables qui façonnent l'avenir!
 La lutte contre le changement climatique est une priorité mondiale. En tant qu’entreprise dont la technologie est utilisée pour alimenter environ 25 % de l’électricité dans le monde, nous prenons notre responsabilité au sérieux. GE Vernova est une entreprise qui prend part à une nouvelle ère énergétique – électrifiant le monde tout en travaillant à le décarboniser. Nous accélérons la transition vers une énergie plus fiable, abordable et durable, tout en aidant nos clients à alimenter des économies et à fournir l'électricité essentielle à la santé, à la sûreté, à la sécurité et à l'amélioration de la qualité de vie.
 L'activité Hydroélectrique de GE Vernova conçoit, développe, fabrique et entretient des technologies avancées qui exploitent la puissance de l'eau pour fournir une énergie fiable et durable. Depuis plus d’un siècle, l’hydroélectricité joue un rôle essentiel dans les systèmes électriques nord-américains et mondiaux. Aujourd’hui, il s’agit de la plus grande source d’énergie renouvelable au monde, et la technologie pompage-turbinage représenta la plus grande source de stockage d’énergie. Mais pour atteindre zéro émission nette à l’échelle mondiale d’ici 2050, nous devons doubler la quantité d’hydroélectricité existante. Que ce soit par pompage-turbinage, au fil de l’eau ou en mettant à niveau la base installée existante, l’hydroélectricité continuera d’être la pierre angulaire de l’avenir énergétique de l’Amérique du Nord.
 Avez-vous l'énergie pour changer le monde ? Si vous êtes prêt à faire la différence et à entrer dans la nouvelle ère énergétique, rejoignez-nous. Vous aurez l'opportunité d'évoluer et de grandir parmi les esprits les plus brillants du secteur, de travailler sur des technologies de pointe et de faire partie d'une équipe mondiale d'environ 75 000 personnes réparties dans plus de 100 pays.

 What you'll do 
 Conduct and lead security research projects across multiple functional areas.
 Identify novel, systemic, and chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.
 Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real-world attack scenarios.
 Assess emerging industry vulnerability classes against the GitLab codebase, and drive remediation of the class rather than the instance.
 Lead security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and define the security requirements that engineering teams build against.
 Build and direct the tooling and automation that scales security research, including agent-assisted vulnerability discovery across our codebase.
 Research the security posture of open source tools and dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our responsible disclosure guidelines .
 Solve technical problems of the highest scope, complexity, and ambiguity.
 Help shape the team and sub-department roadmap.
 Lead the integration of security research results into the engineering and business functions that need to act on them.
 Teach, mentor, and advise other domain experts and individual contributors across several teams.
 Share knowledge and novel vulnerability types with the security community.
 What you'll bring 
 10+ years of experience in security research, penetration testing, or offensive security roles
 Strong ability in discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in large codebase and complex systems
 Proficiency in two or more of Ruby, Go, Python, TypeScript, or Rust. 
 Ability to read and analyze code across multiple languages and codebases
 Strong knowledge of AI frameworks
 Strong understanding of AI attack vectors including prompt injection, agent manipulation, and workflow exploitation
 At ease in establishing and driving complex remediation initiatives involving cross-functional teams
 Excellent written communication skills with an ability to articulate complex topics in a clear and concise manner.
 Ability to translate complex technical findings into clear risk assessments and remediation recommendations
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with creative thinking about attack scenarios

The Role 
 BeyondTrust is seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to help build NHI Governance. NHI Governance is the Pathfinder Insights module that discovers, assesses, and remediates non-human identities — service principals, IAM users, access keys and secrets, workload identities, and AI agents — across Microsoft Entra ID, AWS, and on-premise environments. The system spans .NET 10 services over PostgreSQL; an inventory pipeline fed from governed Databricks lakehouse views; durable Temporal workflows (Python workers, a .NET gateway, protobuf contracts) that onboard, rotate, reduce access for, and decommission live customer credentials, with custody in BeyondTrust Password Safe and storage adapters for AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault; and Angular micro-frontends in the Insights console. It ships through GitOps to Amazon EKS in commercial and government environments.
 You will own how NHI Governance connects to the systems it governs — Microsoft Entra ID, AWS IAM, and vault and PAM platforms including BeyondTrust Password Safe — end to end: the integration code and workflow activities, the least-privilege permissions customers grant us, the setup experience that explains them, the screens that expose them, and the real test environments that prove it all works.
 What You’ll Do
 Build and own integrations with Microsoft Graph (Entra ID), AWS IAM/STS, and vault and PAM platforms — Python workflow activities and .NET services that are idempotent, retry-safe, and compensable.
 Own the per-feature permission matrix: exactly which Graph roles, IAM actions (with resource and condition scoping), and Password Safe permissions each feature needs. Keep it true as the code changes.
 Build the guided setup assets customers run — an Entra setup script, an AWS CloudFormation quick-create, and Password Safe checklists with live verification — and the in-product checks that tell a customer what's missing and how to fix it.
 Own the team's real test environments: Entra test tenants, AWS sandbox accounts, and Password Safe instances, plus the automation that mints, grants, sweeps, and verifies them with least privilege and no standing secrets.
 Own the live end-to-end suites that run governance journeys against real tenants, and debug failures across the API, workflow, vendor API, and permission layers.
 Ship the full stack for what you integrate: .NET APIs over PostgreSQL and the Angular micro-frontend screens for connectors, vault setup, and readiness.
 Be the team's escalation point for opaque vendor failures — the uniform 401s and 403s whose real cause is in an audit log.
 What You’ll Bring 
 Strong backend engineering in Python and C#/.NET — strong in one, working in the other. REST API design. PostgreSQL.
 Hands-on Microsoft Entra ID administration as an engineer: app registrations and service principals, Microsoft Graph application permissions and admin consent, app ownership, managed identities, and federated credentials. You have debugged “why is this 403.”
 AWS IAM in depth: cross-account roles and external ids, policy conditions and resource scoping, STS, Secrets Manager, and SSO/CLI profiles. Comfortable reading and writing Terraform and CloudFormation.
 Experience automating credential lifecycle — creating, rotating, or revoking keys, client secrets, certificates, or vault secrets — with a sound instinct for blast radius.
 Scripting fluency in PowerShell and bash; customers run our setup scripts.
 Working TypeScript and Angular, enough to own a feature's screens in our module-federation micro-frontends.
 Testing against real dependencies, including environment fixtures you set up and tear down yourself.

 Nice To Have
 PAM or vault platform administration: BeyondTrust Password Safe (managed systems, functional accounts, rotation plugins), HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault.
 Temporal or another durable workflow engine; Kafka.

 Daily hands-on practice with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code.
 Who You Are

 Patient with vendor documentation, and good at writing the doc the next person needs.

 The Intake Worker is responsible for providing a welcoming, safe, and supportive first point of contact for youth who are experiencing homelessness, are at immediate risk of homelessness, or require housing-related assistance. Working within a trauma-informed, youth-centered, Housing First for Youth-aligned approach, the Intake Worker responds to all inquiries for services, completes initial screenings and gathering of call data, ensures accurate and timely documentation, identifies immediate safety concerns that require timely escalation, and coordinates access to emergency shelter, diversion, homelessness prevention, and community-based supports.
 HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT  🎯
 Central Intake and Initial Response 
 Serve as a central point of contact for youth seeking emergency shelter, housing assistance, transitional housing access, diversion services or other supports.
 Provide timely response to inquiries and referrals by telephone, email, in person and through designated referral systems.
 Gather relevant information regarding the youth’s immediate circumstances, housing status, presenting needs and current level of risk.
 Maintain accurate call logs and wait lists, as required.
 Provide consistent, accurate, relevant, and timely information in all communications and data sets to support and inform decision-making.
 In consultation with the Diversion team, determine the urgency of each request and prioritize response based on safety, vulnerability and immediate housing needs.
 Screening, Assessment and Service Planning

 Document the youth’s immediate shelter and housing needs, including where the youth stayed previously and where they may be able to safely stay that evening.
 Identify immediate risks related to violence, abuse, human trafficking, mental health, substance use, medical needs, wand other identified risk factors.
 Provide required information to prevention team as required for accurate and timely decision-making, as per youth assignment protocol.
 Information, Referral and Service Navigation 
 Provide relevant referral information about shelter, housing, income, mental health, substance use, health, legal, education, employment, and community services to address the presenting issues of the caller
 Facilitate warm referrals whenever possible rather than only providing contact information.
 Maintain accurate records of referrals and services provided.
 Develop and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and referral sources.
 With the support of the Diversion team, maintain current knowledge of emergency shelters, transitional housing, supportive housing, rental supports, drop-in programs and other youth-serving resources.
 Crisis Intervention and Safety 
 Respond calmly and appropriately to youth experiencing crisis, distress, conflict or heightened emotional states.
 Use de-escalation, active listening, motivational interviewing and crisis-intervention techniques.
 Provide a welcoming, respectful, non-judgmental and youth-friendly response to all individuals seeking assistance.
 Consult with supervisors or appropriate clinical, crisis or emergency services when elevated risks are identified.
 Documentation, Privacy and Data Management 
 Create and maintain accurate, objective and timely electronic and paper records.
 Document inquiries, referrals, admissions, unsuccessful contacts, interventions, and service outcomes.
 Enter information into the organization’s client database, tracking forms, and/or homelessness-management system in accordance with established requirements.
 Protect the confidentiality, privacy and security of youth information.

 Participate in shift exchanges, case consultations, team meetings, training, supervision and program-development activities.
 Maintain professional and collaborative relationships with youth, colleagues, families, community partners and referral sources.
 Follow organizational policies, collective-agreement requirements, health-and-safety practices and professional standards.
 All other duties as required.

SENIOR FULL-STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER, MEDIA

Level: P3
Reporting To: Luc Martel, Director, Engineering 
Location: Ottawa | Hybrid
Type: Permanent | Full-Time

About Solink

Trusted by over 36,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

THE ROLE

As a Senior Full-Stack Engineer on the Media Team, you'll work across Solink's entire media pipeline. It starts with the software that runs on site next to customers' cameras and recorders in more than 36,000 locations. It ends with the AWS-native services that ingest, process, store and serve that media at scale. In between, video is captured, buffered and transcoded at the edge, sent over networks that are often limited or unreliable, and turned into something customers can search, watch and act on in the cloud.

Most of your time will go into the cloud: building media managing/processing services, evolving media APIs, and tuning storage, networking and compute for cost and performance. A large share will also go into the edge: Rust and TypeScript software running on Linux and QTS-based devices, working within tight bandwidth, CPU and storage limits, and keeping thousands of remote devices healthy and up to date. Above all, you'll own the boundary between the two: the protocols, contracts and failure handling that make the pipeline reliable end to end.

This role suits a senior engineer who weighs throughput, latency and cost per gigabyte as carefully as they write code. You're comfortable owning a component from design through production, whether it runs in an AWS region or on a box in a back office you'll never see. You treat reliability and resource efficiency as design constraints from the start. Strong cloud experience is what we value most, but you should be just as comfortable working through what happens on the other side of the network.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, build, and operate media services end to end, from on-site capture, buffering, and upload at the edge to ingestion, processing, storage, and retrieval in the cloud.

 - Work extensively with core AWS services (SQS, S3, Lambda, and related managed services) to build event-driven, loosely coupled pipelines.

 - Build and maintain edge software in Rust and TypeScript running on Linux devices, working within tight bandwidth, CPU, and storage constraints.

 - Design and evolve edge-to-cloud protocols, as well as media platform APIs and contracts for internal and external consumers, with contract and end-to-end tests.

 - Use AI tools effectively throughout the development lifecycle, from planning, design, and implementation to operation, debugging, and observability.

 - Instrument services and devices with meaningful observability: structured logging, metrics, and traces built on OpenTelemetry concepts, so behaviour in production, in the cloud or across a remote fleet, is understandable regardless of the underlying vendor (Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, or otherwise).

 - Own the full deployment lifecycle for your components: staging and production cloud environments, canary releases, and A/B testing, as well as staged roll-outs of edge software.

 - Continuously monitor, tune, and optimize resource usage across cloud and edge (networking, storage tiering, and compute/processing), balancing cost, performance, and reliability trade-offs.

 - Diagnose and resolve complex production issues that span edge devices, customer networks, and cloud services, including intermittent and load-dependent failures in media pipelines.

 - Partner closely with Product, QA, and cross-functional engineering teams to translate media and storage requirements into pragmatic, production-ready solutions.

 - Contribute to architectural decisions for the media platform, including what runs at the edge versus in the cloud, service boundaries, data models, and integration contracts with other teams.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS

 - Strong experience as a senior-level backend or backend-leaning full-stack engineer, with a track record of owning production services end-to-end for low-latency, high-volume data, and solid production experience in TypeScript and/or Rust.

 - Hands-on cloud and AWS experience, with proficiency in core services such as SQS, EKS, Redis, and CloudFront alongside S3/Lambda, and a solid grasp of designing around their operational characteristics and limits.

 - Hands-on experience building software that runs outside the data centre, on Linux or Linux-like devices, with a clear understanding of working within constrained CPU, memory, storage, and bandwidth.

 - Strong networking knowledge (TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT and firewalls, TLS) and experience building reliable data transfer over limited, lossy, or intermittent connections.

 - Strong AI tool usage to increase quality and velocity, and a learning mindset that helps evolve development workflow as AI tooling and capabilities change.

 - Observability experience, not tied to any specific vendor, but a strong conceptual understanding of OpenTelemetry (traces, metrics, logs) and how to use it to make distributed systems and remote devices debuggable.

 - Practical experience with deployment practices: managing staging and production environments, running gradual/canary roll-outs, conducting A/B tests, and safely rolling out updates to remote systems.

 - A resource-aware, optimization-oriented mindset: comfortable fine-tuning networking, storage configuration, and processing pipelines across cloud and edge to balance cost, performance, and reliability.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: asynchronous processing, eventual consistency, idempotency, and failure handling in multi-service pipelines and across unreliable edge-to-cloud links.

 - Comfortable independently diagnosing complex, intermittent production issues across devices, networks, and services, including under pressure.

 - Strong problem-solving skills, an ownership mindset, the ability to influence technical decisions beyond your own code, and comfort improving and extending legacy, brownfield services.

NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Experience with media, video, or other high-throughput binary data pipelines and technologies (e.g. WebRTC, HLS, RTSP, ffmpeg).

 - Experience building or operating OTA update systems, or managing large fleets of remote devices.

 - Experience with QNAP QTS or other NAS/appliance platforms, embedded Linux, cross-compilation, or Linux packaging.

 - Experience with Kubernetes and cloud-native operations (SLOs, incident response), and with GCP or Azure.

 - Experience scaling systems in high-growth or "next-stage" environments.

 - Interest in applying AI/ML to improve product capabilities and team productivity.

CAREER ARCHETYPE ROLE EXPECTATIONS

Career archetypes represent the foundational behaviours and performance standards expected of every employee.

At Solink, career archetypes define the baseline for how we show up and create impact. They are not aspirational traits or optional strengths, they are the minimum standards required to operate successfully within our environment. These expectations ensure consistency in how we think, collaborate, execute, and raise the performance bar. If someone consistently does not meet these standards, they are not aligned with what it takes to thrive at Solink.

This is a P3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level independently own initiatives from start to finish with minimal direction. They proactively solve problems, collaborate across functions, and prioritize their work based on business needs and expected impact.

 - Propose, launch, and deliver initiatives aligned with team and company goals.

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

COMPENSATION

The salary range for this role is $115,837 - $165,000 CAD.

We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role as identified during the interview process, and by what will be expected of you by day 90.

For this position, our goal is to hire a candidate who possesses the relevant skills at any level below:

 - Developing: Foundational, relevant experience and skills, with the ability to build capability in the role through hands-on experience, coaching, and support.

Job Title: Staff Supply Chain Simulation Scientist
 Primary Job Location: Hybrid, three days per week, Toronto / Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Ontario, Canada
 Employment Type: Permanent, Full-Time
 Hiring Timeline: Immediate
 Reporting Line: Chief Scientist
 Existing Vacancy: Yes
 Compensation: $145,000 - $170,000 CAD per year with a 12 percent target bonus.
 About Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) 
 Fulfillment IQ is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations.
 We work at the intersection of strategy, supply chain, and technology where we solve complex, real-world problems across warehouse design, automation, order management, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain execution.
 Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk.
 If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is the place where your skills and judgment truly come to life.
 Role Overview 
 Workbench is FIQ's warehouse-design platform: it lets a solutions engineer draw a warehouse the way an architect draws a building. You will design, build and own Workbench’s warehouse simulation engine, wherein a warehouse design is simulated and evaluated against multiple operational scenarios. Reporting directly to the Chief Scientist, you will create simulation models that capture warehouse operations dynamics, design and build the engine that executes them, and lead its integration into our main product.
 This is a unique opportunity to build something from scratch, assemble a team, and have a direct influence on product features and technical roadmap. You will work closely with our Chief Scientist, domain experts, and developers to build a capability that does not exit. It is a genuine zero-to-one build, and you will own the simulation vertical as it grows.
 What You'll Do
 Translate warehouse operational processes into mathematical simulation models at various levels of granularity
 Identify the right simulation paradigm (or combination thereof) for the problem at hand and the best tools to solve it. 
 Benchmark the performance of the simulation engine across various types of warehouse operations
 Drive the discussion around simulation as a product by prioritizing features, establishing a technical and product roadmap, and overseeing development and integration efforts.
 Assemble and lead the team that will help build and maintain the simulation engine 
 Lean on AI tools for execution and spend your judgment on the ambiguous parts. 
 The Honest Version of the Hard Parts 
 This is genuinely zero-to-one. There is no reference tool to copy and no clean spec to build from, so the hardest part is the ambiguity. You will often start without a clear definition of what to build and will have to think your way through it. 
 Your models will shape how real warehouses get designed. All models have limitations, so it is important to be honest about what they capture and what they don’t.
 You are the lead. You carry the open questions and the vertical, not just the modeling, and you will switch context fast as the product takes shape.
 Where This Goes 
 Think chessboard, not ladder.  You will own and grow the simulation vertical, and there is real room to move into deeper research alongside the Chief Scientist and into a broader product and platform role. Tell us what you want to build and we will help you get there.
 How We'll Interview You 
 Intro conversation: a short call to swap context and make sure the basics line up.
 Conversation with the Chief Scientist: a first call on how you think. 
 Technical: a scripted, comparable working session on a real simulation problem. How you frame it, model it, handle missing information, and defend it. 
 Final: discussion with the Workbench team.
 What You Need to Have 
 5+ years, capable of architecting simulation solutions, not just operating simulation tools.
 Experience and understanding of warehouse operations, material handling, robotics, conveyors, AMRs, and automation.
 Strong experience with discrete-event simulation (DES), AnyLogic, FlexSim, Siemens Plant Simulation, or similar.
 Experience with Python, simulation frameworks (SimPy, etc.).
 Hands-on experience in designing and building simulation models, with a good understanding of different simulation paradigms and when to use (or not to use) them.
 Comfort in a zero-to-one, high-ambiguity environment, and the thinking to move forward when the problem is not yet defined.
 Experience with NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, OpenUSD, CAD-to-3D workflows.
 Strong engineering ability to build the models and the tooling around them, with AI leaned on for the execution.
 A Master's or PhD in Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Computer Science, or a related field, or a Bachelor's with equivalent hands-on simulation experience.
 Nice to have: Warehouse automation, robotics, or material-handling exposure.
 Nice to have: Experience owning a technical vertical or setting standards on a small team.
 Why You Will Love Working Here 
 You will build the simulation practice, not inherit someone else's. This means real ownership on a team small enough that your judgment sets the standard, working directly with the Chief Scientist to build something that does not exist yet. You will be part of a team with domain experts and developers who support each other in achieving our goals. We move fast, we automate the busywork, and we back people who take initiative.

Si vous êtes curieux, motivé par les défis complexes et passionné par la transformation de l'innovation produit en impact commercial, ce poste est fait pour vous.

ABOUT VALPAY 
 Founded in 2022, ValPay is an all-in-one payment solution tailored to empower its partners' software platforms. Designed for ambitious business owners wanting to focus on growing their business rather than the logistics needed to run it, ValPay helps companies prevent fraud, gain access to real-time reporting, and accept both online and in-person payments. ValPay's PayFac-as-a-Service model gives its partners all the benefits of integrated payments while handling the heavy lifting.
 ValPay is a subsidiary of Valsoft.
 THE ROLE 
 As Head of Engineering, you will own the engineering organization at ValPay — how it is structured, how it delivers, and how good it gets. You will report to the CEO and work alongside product and go-to-market leadership to turn a talented, lean team into a predictable, high-performing engineering function.
 This is a build role, not a caretaker role. ValPay's engineering team has grown quickly and now needs someone to put real operating discipline behind it: a delivery rhythm people can count on, a management layer that holds, and technical standards that let the platform scale with the business — without losing the speed and hands-on energy that got ValPay here.
 We are hiring for trajectory. This role is scoped as Head of Engineering today, and it is designed as the potential path to Chief Technology Officer at ValPay. We would rather hire someone with the ceiling to grow into that seat and back them properly than hire the title and hope. What earns the step up is straightforward: a delivery organization that runs without heroics, a leadership bench you built, and a track record of technical judgment the CEO and the board can lean on.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 Own engineering delivery end to end — planning, execution, release cadence, and quality — and make it predictable enough that the business can plan around it.
 Build and lead the engineering management layer: hire, develop, and coach engineering managers, tech leads, and senior/staff engineers, and put a durable structure beneath you.
 Partner with Product on roadmap feasibility, sequencing, and trade-offs. Product sets the what; you own the how and the when.
 Set and enforce technical standards across the platform — architecture, code quality, testing, observability, and documentation — so the system scales as GMV and merchant count grow.
 Serve as the senior technical escalation point for integrations with core payments partners (Adyen, Fiserv), working complex issues to resolution and feeding what you learn back into the platform.
 Drive AI adoption inside engineering — in the SDLC, in developer productivity, and in the product where it measurably improves outcomes.
 Own engineering operations and reliability: on-call, incident response, postmortems, and the SLAs a PCI DSS Level 1 payments platform has to hold.
 Partner with security and compliance to keep PCI DSS certification and multi-jurisdiction obligations met as the platform expands.
 Be a steady presence under pressure, and build the organizational muscle for the team to handle incidents increasingly without you.
 WHAT YOU BRING 
 8+ years in software engineering, including 4+ years leading engineering teams, with at least some of that time managing managers or tech leads.
 Proven experience building, structuring, and scaling technology organizations, ideally in high-growth environments.
 Experience hiring and developing engineering leaders, and the appetite to keep doing it.
 You can still apply hands-on technical depth, you review architecture, you can go deep in a design review or an incident, and engineers respect your judgment. You are not expected to write production code day to day.
 Strong judgment on build-versus-buy, technical debt, and where to spend engineering capacity — and the ability to explain those calls in business terms to a non-technical executive team.
 A track record of installing delivery process in a fast-moving team without killing its speed: planning cadence, release discipline, on-call, and the metrics to know whether it is working.
 Demonstrable ambition and ceiling. You want the CTO seat eventually and you can show what you have been doing to get ready for it.
 NICE TO HAVE 
 Payments, fintech, or other regulated/high-availability environments (PCI DSS, SOC 2, or similar).
 Experience in a high-growth or private-equity-backed environment, or integrating engineering teams from acquisitions.
 Experience with multi-tenant platform or API-first product architecture.
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE 
 In the first six to twelve months:
 A management layer is in place: engineering managers or tech leads owning their areas, with clear scope and accountability.
 Engineering runs on a delivery rhythm the business can plan against — commitments are made and met, and slippage is visible early rather than at the deadline.
 Delivery and reliability are measured, not felt — baseline metrics exist for throughput, lead time, change failure rate, and incident response, and they are trending the right way.
 AI is in real use inside engineering, with live use cases rather than pilots.
 On-call and incident response are defined and drilled, and incidents are increasingly resolved without you in the room.
 Technical standards and architecture direction are written down, agreed, and actually followed.
 WHY VALPAY 
 Founded in 2022, ValPay is already operating at scale: a PCI DSS Level 1 certified platform running across 40+ jurisdictions in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, serving vertical software platforms in dental, marine, property management, automotive, and more.
 Growth runs on three engines, and all three run on the same platform:
 Internal sales — converting existing Valsoft GMV to ValPay, a $15B+ opportunity across the current customer base plus every new Valsoft acquisition.
 External ISV channel — signing ISVs outside the Valsoft portfolio, $25M–$50M in revenue, with $2B+ in deals already closed and now being converted into live, processing merchants.
 M&A engine — acquiring payment gateway businesses, two closed so far, with the same conversion playbook applied to each newly acquired asset.
 Embedded payments inside a portfolio of 150+ vertical software companies is distribution most payments companies spend years trying to build. ValPay already has it. What decides how fast these engines scale is the engineering organization behind them — which is the mandate of this role.
 ValPay is backed by Valsoft, which buys and holds companies indefinitely rather than selling them. You build on a long horizon, not toward an exit.
 For more information: https://www.valpay.com/ 
___________________________________________________________________________________________
 À PROPOS DE VALPAY 
 Fondée en 2022, ValPay est une solution de paiement tout-en-un conçue pour outiller les plateformes logicielles de ses partenaires. Pensée pour les entrepreneurs ambitieux qui souhaitent se consacrer à la croissance de leur entreprise plutôt qu'à la logistique nécessaire à son exploitation, ValPay aide les entreprises à prévenir la fraude, à accéder à des rapports en temps réel et à accepter les paiements en ligne comme en personne. Le modèle de facilitation des paiements en tant que service (PayFac-as-a-Service) de ValPay procure à ses partenaires tous les avantages des paiements intégrés, tout en prenant en charge le gros du travail.
 ValPay est une filiale de Valsoft.
 LE POSTE 
 À titre de chef de l'ingénierie, vous prendrez en charge l'organisation d'ingénierie de ValPay : sa structure, sa capacité de livraison et son niveau d'excellence. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez aux côtés des responsables du produit et de la mise en marché afin de transformer une équipe talentueuse et restreinte en une fonction d'ingénierie prévisible et très performante.
 Il s'agit d'un rôle de bâtisseur, et non de gestionnaire de statu quo. L'équipe d'ingénierie de ValPay a connu une croissance rapide et a maintenant besoin d'une personne capable d'y instaurer une véritable discipline opérationnelle : une cadence de livraison fiable, une couche de gestion solide et des normes techniques permettant à la plateforme d'évoluer au rythme de l'entreprise — sans perdre la rapidité et l'énergie concrète qui ont mené ValPay jusqu'ici.
 Nous recrutons pour le potentiel. Ce poste est défini aujourd'hui comme celui de chef de l'ingénierie, et il est conçu comme la voie d'accès possible au poste de chef de la technologie (CTO) chez ValPay. Nous préférons embaucher une personne ayant la capacité de croître vers ce rôle et l'appuyer pleinement, plutôt que d'embaucher un titre en espérant que cela fonctionne. Les conditions de cette progression sont claires : une organisation de livraison qui fonctionne sans héroïsme, un banc de leaders que vous aurez bâti, et un jugement technique sur lequel la direction et le conseil peuvent s'appuyer.

 Assumer la livraison en ingénierie de bout en bout — planification, exécution, cadence de mise en production et qualité — et la rendre suffisamment prévisible pour que l'entreprise puisse planifier en conséquence.
 Bâtir et diriger la couche de gestion en ingénierie : embaucher, développer et encadrer des gestionnaires de l'ingénierie, des chefs techniques et des ingénieurs seniors ou principaux, et mettre en place une structure durable sous votre responsabilité.
 Collaborer avec le Produit sur la faisabilité, le séquencement et les compromis de la feuille de route. Le Produit définit le quoi; vous êtes responsable du comment et du quand.

 Agir comme point d'escalade technique senior pour les intégrations avec les principaux partenaires de paiement (Adyen, Fiserv), en menant les enjeux complexes jusqu'à leur résolution et en réinjectant les apprentissages dans la plateforme.
 Piloter l'adoption de l'IA au sein de l'ingénierie — dans le cycle de développement, dans la productivité des développeurs et dans le produit lorsque les bénéfices sont mesurables.
 Assumer les opérations d'ingénierie et la fiabilité : garde, réponse aux incidents, post-mortems et niveaux de service qu'exige une plateforme de paiement certifiée PCI DSS de niveau 1.
 Collaborer avec les équipes de sécurité et de conformité afin de maintenir la certification PCI DSS et les obligations multijuridictionnelles à mesure que la plateforme s'étend.
 Demeurer une présence stable sous pression et développer la capacité organisationnelle permettant à l'équipe de gérer les incidents de plus en plus sans vous.
 CE QUE VOUS APPORTEZ 
 Au moins 8 ans d'expérience en génie logiciel, dont 4 ans ou plus à diriger des équipes d'ingénierie, incluant une période de gestion de gestionnaires ou de chefs techniques.
 Expérience démontrée dans la création, la structuration et la mise à l'échelle d'organisations technologiques, idéalement dans des environnements à forte croissance.
 Expérience d'embauche et de développement de leaders en ingénierie, et le désir de continuer à le faire.
 Vous conservez une profondeur technique concrète et applicable : vous révisez l'architecture, vous pouvez approfondir une revue de conception ou un incident, et les ingénieurs respectent votre jugement. L'écriture de code en production au quotidien n'est pas attendue.
 Un jugement solide sur les décisions de type « développer ou acheter », sur la dette technique et sur l'allocation de la capacité d'ingénierie — et la capacité d'expliquer ces choix en termes d'affaires à une équipe de direction non technique.
 Un historique démontré d'implantation de processus de livraison dans une équipe qui avance vite, sans en freiner la rapidité : cadence de planification, discipline de mise en production, garde, et les indicateurs permettant d'en mesurer l'efficacité.
 Une ambition et un potentiel démontrables. Vous visez éventuellement le poste de chef de la technologie et vous pouvez démontrer ce que vous faites pour vous y préparer.
 ATOUTS RECHERCHÉS 
 Expérience dans les paiements, en technologie financière ou dans d'autres environnements réglementés à haute disponibilité (PCI DSS, SOC 2 ou équivalent).
 Expérience dans un environnement à forte croissance ou détenu par un fonds d'investissement privé, ou en intégration d'équipes d'ingénierie issues d'acquisitions.
 Expérience des architectures de plateforme multilocataire ou de produits axés sur les API.
 CE À QUOI RESSEMBLE LA RÉUSSITE 
 Au cours des six à douze premiers mois :
 Une couche de gestion est en place : des gestionnaires de l'ingénierie ou des chefs techniques responsables de leurs domaines, avec un périmètre et une imputabilité clairs.
 L'ingénierie fonctionne selon une cadence de livraison sur laquelle l'entreprise peut planifier : les engagements sont pris et tenus, et les écarts sont visibles tôt plutôt qu'à l'échéance.
 La livraison et la fiabilité sont mesurées, et non ressenties : des indicateurs de référence existent pour le débit, le délai de livraison, le taux d'échec des changements et la réponse aux incidents, et ils évoluent dans la bonne direction.
 L'IA est utilisée concrètement au sein de l'ingénierie, avec des cas d'utilisation en production plutôt que des projets pilotes.
 La garde et la réponse aux incidents sont définies et exercées, et les incidents se règlent de plus en plus sans votre présence.
 Les normes techniques et l'orientation architecturale sont documentées, acceptées et réellement appliquées.

 Moteur d'acquisitions — acquérir des entreprises de passerelles de paiement : deux transactions conclues à ce jour, le même plan de conversion étant appliqué à chaque actif acquis.
 Offrir des paiements intégrés au sein d'un portefeuille de plus de 150 sociétés de logiciels verticaux représente un réseau de distribution que la plupart des entreprises de paiement mettent des années à bâtir. ValPay le possède déjà. Ce qui déterminera la vitesse de ces trois moteurs, c'est l'organisation d'ingénierie qui les soutient — et c'est là le mandat de ce poste.

ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As a Senior Program Manager, PMO, you will own program management for Juniper Square’s most complex, cross-functional software initiatives, driving execution from planning through release while acting as a senior voice inside our Program Management Office (PMO). You will partner closely with engineering, product, design, QA, platform, and operations leadership to build program plans, resolve dependencies, and keep delivery on track against customer commitments. You will act as a bridge between engineering, product management, and other cross-functional partners, translating ambiguous, high-stakes problems into a program plan that accounts for internal and external dependencies.

Beyond your own programs, you will help set the standard for how the PMO runs: contributing to governance, process standardization, metrics, and, critically, how the team uses AI. This role carries a heavy AI focus. You are expected to operate at the Workflow Orchestrator level on Juniper Square’s AI fluency ladder. That means you do not just use AI tools yourself; you design and deploy multi-step workflows that span multiple tools or data sources and replace manual coordination, and you build the reusable systems (prompt libraries, Cowork skills and plugins, scripted Jira/Confluence data extraction) that other program and technical program managers across the org rely on. You will be looked to as the AI thought leader for the PMO organization, actively raising the AI fluency floor for the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own program management for Juniper Square’s most complex, multi-team software initiatives, partnering with engineering, product, design, QA, platform, and operations to build program plans, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and drive execution through every stage of the software development lifecycle.

 - Act as a senior bridge between engineering and product management, translating ambiguous, cross-functional problems into a concrete program plan with clear milestones, owners, and dependencies, including with third-party teams where relevant.

 - Establish and evolve the execution framework (agile/scrum ceremonies, artifacts, governance cadence) for your programs, and contribute those improvements back into PMO-wide standards and processes.

 - Provide regular, senior-leadership-ready status reporting; proactively identify, monitor, and mitigate risk; apply change management discipline when scope or timelines shift.

 - Contribute to PMO governance, including metrics definitions, process standardization, and adherence tracking, across the broader program management team.

 - Design and deploy multi-step, AI-powered workflows, such as Cowork skills and plugins and scripted Jira/Confluence extraction and analysis, that replace manual PMO coordination, built as systems other PMs and TPMs can reuse rather than one-off personal shortcuts.

 - Maintain a working library of reusable prompts, templates, and automations for high-frequency PMO work (status reporting, metrics dashboards, roadmap artifacts) and proactively share them across the team.

 - Serve as an AI thought leader for the PMO org: define what “good” looks like before automating a workflow, build in validation steps, and own the accuracy of anything you ship. You can delegate the work, never the accountability.

 - Mentor and coach TPMs and PMs on day-to-day program management practice, PMO goals, and their own AI fluency; contribute to roadmap planning and help anticipate delivery challenges across the organization.

 - Ensure program documentation, status reporting, and delivery metrics are maintained on a regular, reliable cadence.
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

 - 15+ years of total industry experience, including 8+ years of technical program management on complex, large programs spanning multiple cross-functional teams.

 - Deep understanding of the product development lifecycle and technical program management at scale, with a track record of driving programs from concept through release across multiple teams.

 - Demonstrated AI fluency at the Workflow Orchestrator level: you have designed and deployed at least one multi-step AI or Cowork workflow spanning multiple tools or data sources, with a measurable time or quality improvement you can speak to specifically. Not just personal, ad hoc prompting.

 - Comfortable maintaining a working library of reusable prompts, skills, or workflow templates, and configuring Cowork skills, connectors, and plugins without needing engineering support.

 - Hands-on experience automating program-management workflows with AI, for example scripting or using AI tools to extract and analyze data from Jira and Confluence, generate status reports, or build reusable prompt libraries and templates that others rely on.

 - Comfort defining quality criteria before deploying AI-assisted workflows, validating outputs, and owning the accuracy of anything you automate.

 - Experience with program and project governance: budgeting, vendor management, compliance, and metrics.

 - Professional credentials (PMI PMP, ACP, CSM) a plus.

 - Experience with fintech platforms, cloud platforms (AWS), Docker, and Kubernetes a plus.

 - Self-driven and adaptable, comfortable mentoring peers, and flexible working with counterparts across geographies and time zones.
   
   

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary and equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $190,000 USD.
